_about: Brinewick: the harbour south of Route 3, Trial Hall #3 (Master Marisol, TIDE, Seal 3), the Glimmerwell depot with the Faded Drizzlet (D165), Dorian Pell's first battle, and the Episode 1 card. One auto-loaded detail pack. Role names (Lantern Host, Chandler, Deckhand, Bell Ringer, Net Mender, Ferry Hand, Harbour Clerk) and all lines are marked placeholder copy until Design signs them. objs.deny: The Hall is shut. A chalk note: 'Down on the quay. Back with the tide. M.'

objs.text: BRINEWICK · A harbour town. Ferry at the west pier. Please mind the nets.
BRINEWICK TRIAL HALL · Master Marisol · TIDE · "The tide keeps time."
BRINEWICK DOCKS · A Glimmerwell Co. depot. Brighter by nature.

lines.else: A bench facing the sea. Salt has bleached it soft.
Nets drying in the wind. A float is tangled in the corner.
Wet rope, coiled the sailor's way.
The ferry's mooring post. The rope is slack. She's in for the day.
The windsock points out to sea.
A sealed crate stamped BRINEWICK DOCKS. It hums a little.
Glimmerwell crates, stacked perfectly square.

lines.story.brine_dorian: Dorian walked right past me. He looked smaller up close.
lines.story.brine_freed: You opened it. ...Okay. Okay. I'm staying close.
lines.else: The depot's east, past the square. The hum is louder over there.

lines.story.ep1_end: Three Seals, and you still stop to talk to an old net mender. Good.
lines.story.brine_freed: Heard a cage came open in the depot. The gulls went quiet. They do that for good news.
lines.else: The company pays well for dock work. The crates hum, though. Nets don't hum.

lines.story.side=glimmer: Glimmerwell leases the east pier. The rest of the harbour is still ours, holder.
lines.else: The east pier is leased to the company. The rest of the harbour is still the town's.

lines.story.seal3: The captain hums when she's pleased. She's been humming since your match.
lines.else: The captain runs the ferry and the Hall. Same rule for both: the tide keeps time.

The house lantern, on gimbals like a ship's. It swings a little in the wind.

A kettle on a little stove. Someone always keeps it warm.

objs.text: A note by the door: "Rest a while. Dry coats on the left. A rest costs a few Acorns. Brinewick"

lines.else: Rope, tins, snacks for the road. If it floats or it feeds, I sell it.
The counter is an old boat hull, upside down.
A brass scale. It's honest, and a little green.
Oars and boat hooks, sorted by length.
Lamp oil. The company sells a cleaner kind. Nobody here buys it.
A net on the wall, with orange floats caught in it.
A spare buoy, freshly painted.

lines.else: Quarter close is with me, partner. The captain is optional.
The ferry bell. Marisol rings it when the tide turns.
A tide chart, inked by hand. The beats are marked like music.

bw_arrive: Salt wind and ferry bells. Brinewick's roofs lean toward the water.
{name}! You made it. I got here with the cart. I watched every crate come off.
They all went into that white shed on the east pier. One of them hums. Nobody here seems to hear it.
No lanyard, no clipboard. I can still walk in there with you. Let's look.
{name}. Delivery's done. Twelve crates, all signed. I kept my lanyard straight the whole ride.
They went into the depot on the east pier. One still hums. Dorian calls it a routine unit.
You're on the count too, right? Look at that one crate. Then tell me it's routine.
Lantern House is just west of the square. Rest first. The depot is east, by the quay.
bw_hollis: {name}. Hollis, Brinewick count. I took the quarry job, then they sent me here.
I counted. The lamps don't count glow. This crate doesn't hold glow. It holds someone.
The cage by the far wall. I can't open it. I can look at this wall for a while, though.
bw_hollis@glimmer: Partner. Hollis, Brinewick count. Dorian wants the manifest signed by a holder.
Twelve lines. Eleven are lamps. Line twelve is the cage by the wall. Grey. Breathing.
Sign it and it ships at dusk. Or look first. I won't write down which.
bw_crate: A Glimmer Cell crate. Bars, not boards. A grey Drizzlet curls on the mesh, its glow very low.
{pet} presses its nose to the bars. The Drizzlet's tail twitches once.
The latch is stiff. {pet} leans in with you, and the lid swings up.
bw_crate@glimmer: A Glimmer Cell crate. Bars, not boards. A grey Drizzlet curls on the mesh, its glow very low.
{pet} presses its nose to the bars. The manifest on the desk says: LINE 12, UNIT, TIDE.
You sign. THUNK. The stamp leaves a bright mint star on the cage.
Signed. ...It's too grey to ship, partner. Rejected stock. Policy says the holder keeps it.
You leave the pen on the desk and lift the latch. The lid swings up.
I didn't see that. Dorian will. It will cost you on the board.
bw_drizzlet_meet: The Drizzlet stays close. A little blue creeps back into its tail.
The Drizzlet huddles in the open crate. It isn't ready yet. Come back gently.
bw_drizzlet_again: The grey Drizzlet watches you from the open crate.
bw_dorian: Ah. The holder from Cobblecrest. You opened company property, {name}.
That unit was a partnership in progress. You've turned it into a loss.
No more smiles today. Show me what a Keeper thinks a Walkling is for.
bw_dorian@glimmer: Junior Bright! The count came in with a loose line. Let's call this your quarterly review.
Out here on the quay, in public. The Capital likes a holder who can win where people watch.
bw_dorian_win: Units, holders, partners. You keep picking the wrong word on purpose.
The captain has her Hall open on the west pier. Go on. The tide won't wait for me either.
Dorian walks off down the quay. He does not say have a bright day.
bw_dorian_win@glimmer: Review passed. Your file says strong, and stubborn. Both sell.
Quinn is in the Hall on the west pier. Close the quarter there, or test the captain if you like.
marisol_trial: The tide's out, {name}. Sit a while. The ferry bell will tell us when it turns.
Hale sent you? Then say it. ...Ha. That old stone still owes me a ferry ride.
On my deck the tide comes in on a beat. The faster Walkling moves first. Show me you can read it.
marisol_trial@glimmer: Tier 3 is on file. The tide can keep its own schedule.
Quarter close, partner. Dorian passed your review on the quay. That is enough for Tier 3.
The company rents my floor for its paperwork. My deck still runs on the tide.
How do you close the quarter?
seal3: That's the Brinewick Seal. An anchor, so you always find your way back.
Tell Hale the tide still remembers him. And tell your Walkling it read the beat well.
seal3@glimmer: Quarter closed. Bright Tier 3 Lanyard. Three marks, one cord.
The Capital will want to meet you. Not today. Today, rest.
gauge_a: A tide gauge in the gap. Paint on the post asks: THE TIDE COMES IN. WHO MOVES FIRST?
The water parts around the post. Higher SPD acts first. On a tie, the tide picks.
The water stays put. Size doesn't set the turn. Speed does.
The water laps at your boots. Waiting only lets the faster one go first.
gauge_b: Another gauge. Paint: THE TIDE IS FASTER THAN YOU. HOW DO YOU GET AHEAD OF IT?
The water draws back. Moves that raise your SPD put you first next turn.
The water draws back. Slow the foe's SPD and the turn swings to you.
The water holds. A harder hit still lands second. Change the speed instead.
bw_ep1_end: That's three, {name}. You and {pet} did it. I watched the whole match through a porthole.
That Drizzlet's colour is coming back. Lizzy will want to see. So will my mom.
Three marks, colleague. Dorian clapped. I clapped. ...The Drizzlet's colour is coming back, though.
Units don't get their colour back. Walklings do. I'm writing that down somewhere.
The ferry turns at the bell. Wherever the Amberwild sends you next, come back by sea.
Far up the coast, a tall grey tower rises on a ridge. Above it, the clouds go flat and still.
EPISODE 1 COMPLETE · Thank you for playing Walklings!

lines.win: Noted. You win in public. I'll have to remember that.
lines.lose: A loss is just a delay with bad lighting. Rest, then try me again.

lines.intro: Quarterly review, Junior Bright. Smile for the quay.
lines.win: Strong numbers. Stubborn, too. The Capital likes both.
lines.lose: The review stays open. Rest, and bring better numbers.

lines.intro: The tide keeps time. Let's see if you can keep up with it.
lines.win: You read the beat, {player}. The tide goes out for you.
lines.lose: The tide's in. Rest, and come back when it turns.

lines.intro: The company's paper can wait. My deck can't. Show me your beat.
lines.win: You read the tide. Tell Quinn the quarter closed itself.
lines.lose: The tide's in. Quinn will still take your paperwork.

lines.intro: Mind the wash! First one to move wins the deck.
lines.win: You were quicker on the beat, {player}. Fair tide.
lines.lose: The tide caught you. Rest, then try the deck again.

lines.intro: When the bell rings, the fast one goes first. Ready?
lines.win: Rung out! You've got the captain's timing.
lines.lose: Off the beat. Rest, then listen for the bell.
